name: Myrinus
bio: Myrinus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the first volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Books I–VI) (Book VI: 108, 254).

poems.title: Book VI, 108
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text: Yet Pans, keepers of the high mountains, ye jolly horned dancers, lords of grassy Arcady, make Diotimus rich in sheep and goats, accepting the gifts of his splendid sacrifice.

poems.title: Book VI, 254
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text: When Time was about to drag down to Hades pathic Statyllius, the effeminate old stump of Aphrodite, he dedicated in the porch of Priapus his light summer dresses dyed in scarlet and crimson, his false hair greasy with spikenard, his white shoes that shone on his shapely ankles, the chest in which reposed his bombasine frippery, and his flute that breathed sweet music in the revels of the harlot tribe.

poems.title: Book VII, 703: Not Sepulchral
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text: Thyrsis the villager who feeds the Nymphs’ flocks, Thyrsis whose piping is equal to Pan’s, sleeps under the shady pine tree having drunk wine at midday, and Love takes his crook and keeps the flock himself. Ye Nymphs ye Nymphs awake the shepherd who fears no wolf, lest Love become the prey of wild beasts.

poems.title: Book XI, 67
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text: The letter v signifies four hundred, but your years are twice as much, my tender Lais, as old as a crow and Hecuba put together, grandmother of Sisyphus and sister of Deucalion. But dye your white hair and say “tata” to everyone.

poems.title: The Shepherd of the Nymphs (Mackail)
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Thyrsis the reveller, the shepherd of the Nymphs' sheep, Thyrsis who pipes on the reed like Pan, having drunk at noon, sleeps under the shady pine, and Love himself has taken his crook and watches the flocks.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.108: Ὑψηλῶν ὀρέων
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text:
Ὑψηλῶν ὀρέων ἔφοροι, κεραοὶ χοροπαῖκται,
Πᾶνες, βουχίλου κράντορες Ἀρκαδίης,
εὔαρνον θείητε καὶ εὐχίμαρον Διότιμον,
δεξάμενοι λαμπρῆς δῶρα θυηπολίης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.254: Τὴν μαλακὴν Παφίης
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text:
Τὴν μαλακὴν Παφίης Στατύλλιον ἀνδρόγυνον δρῦν
ἕλκειν εἰς Ἀίδην ἡνίκʼ ἔμελλε χρόνος,
τὰκ κόκκου βαφθέντα καὶ ὑσγίνοιο θέριστρα,
καὶ τοὺς ναρδολιπεῖς ἀλλοτρίους πλοκάμους,
φαικάδα τʼ εὐτάρσοισιν ἐπʼ ἀστραγάλοισι γελῶσαν,
καὶ τὴν γρυτοδόκην κοιτίδα παμβακίδων,
αὐλοὺς θʼ ἡδὺ πνέοντας ἑταιρείοις ἐνὶ κώμοις,
δῶρα Πριηπείων θῆκεν ἐπὶ προθύρων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.703: Θύρσις ὁ κωμήτης
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text:
Θύρσις ὁ κωμήτης, ὁ τὰ νυμφικὰ μῆλα νομεύων,
Θύρσις ὁ συρίζων Πανὸς ἴσον δόνακι,
ἔνδιος οἰνοπότης σκιερὰν ὑπὸ τὰν πίτυν εὕδει·
φρουρεῖ δʼ αὐτὸς ἑλὼν ποίμνια βάκτρον Ἔρως.
ἆ Νύμφαι, Νύμφαι, διεγείρατε τὸν λυκοθαρσῆ
βοσκόν, μὴ θηρῶν κύρμα γένηται Ἔρως.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XI.67: Ὑ τετρηκόσιʼ ἐστίν
poems.author: Myrinus
poems.text:
Ὑ τετρηκόσιʼ ἐστίν· ἔχεις δὲ σὺ τοὺς ἐνιαυτοὺς
δὶς τόσσους, τρυφερὴ Λαΐ κορωνεκάβη,
Σισύφου ὦ μάμμη, καὶ Δευκαλίωνος ἀδελφή.
βάπτε δὲ τὰς λευκάς, καὶ λέγε πᾶσι τατᾶ.
